html: The Badimaya, also written Badimia, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Mid West of Western Australia, in the country around Mount Magnet, Yalgoo and Paynes Find. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their neighbours were the Wajarri to the north, the Amangu and Nhanda toward the coast, and the Kalaamaya to the southeast. The Murchison gold rush of the early 1890s brought mining towns onto their land, and sheep stations followed. Their language is endangered, and work has been done to record and teach it.
